review.alternative: Passive degrees of freedom might serve as reservoirs that increase total system-wide entropy production if coupling is strong.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing that non-driven degrees of freedom consistently increase dissipation in specific Langevin regimes.

claims.statement: Entropy production in driven overdamped Langevin systems can be effectively upper-bounded by the statistics of driven particles alone, with passive degrees of freedom contributing to reduced dissipation.

support.explanation: Passive degrees of freedom constrain the entropy production rate, providing an analytical route to bound dissipation without needing full system state information.
support.passage: We use this finding to argue that the presence of non-driven, passive degrees of freedom generally leads to decreased dissipation.

review.alternative: Non-reciprocal effects may be negligible in high-temperature environments where thermal noise dominates.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical data showing no statistically significant modulation of efficiency across varying degrees of non-reciprocal coupling.

claims.statement: Non-reciprocal couplings in autonomous information engines can significantly modulate inter-dot information flow, potentially optimizing energy conversion efficiency.

support.explanation: Non-reciprocal couplings offer a mechanism for directed information transfer, which is pivotal for the operation of autonomous information engines.
support.passage: nonreciprocity can significantly modulate the inter-dot inf

actions.findings:
Entropy production in driven overdamped Langevin systems can be effectively upper-bounded by the statistics of driven particles alone, with passive degrees of freedom contributing to reduced dissipation. [peer-30b9153ce0fe31018c8e3730]

Non-reciprocal couplings in autonomous information engines can significantly modulate inter-dot information flow, potentially optimizing energy conversion efficiency. [peer-f3ee30889b8396e02ea0588a]
actions.limitations: Current findings rely primarily on overdamped Langevin models and autonomous double-quantum-dot architectures; high-inertia regimes and fully non-Markovian dynamics remain speculative.
actions.next_questions: Determine if the thermodynamic benefits of non-reciprocal coupling generalize to larger networks of coupled information processors.
actions.reason: Incorporating recent peer-reviewed bounds on entropy production and non-reciprocal coupling dynamics to refine the project's understanding of dissipation.
actions.summary: This revision synthesizes findings on entropy production bounds and the role of non-reciprocal couplings in autonomous information engines, establishing that predictive information and passive degrees of freedom provide concrete upper bounds on dissipation in driven systems.
actions.title: Predictive Dissipation and Information Engines (Revised)
